Definition: from G4253 and G2983; to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise:--come aforehand, overtake, take before.
BiblicalUsage: Prolambano means to take in advance, to take before others. Jesus' anointing woman came beforehand to anoint his body, and Paul rebukes the Corinthians because every one takes before others his own supper.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe taking beforehand can be love or selfishness, and the same act is judged by whose need it serves.
